# Vendored crates

Copies of published crates carried with patches until the patches are taken upstream. Each is wired in through `[patch.crates-io]` in the workspace `Cargo.toml` and excluded from the workspace, so it builds under its own settings and `cargo fmt --all` leaves it alone. Every change to a copy is marked with a `KOAN:` comment; `grep -rn KOAN: vendor/` lists them.

`vendor/patches/<crate>.patch` is each copy's change from its crates.io release, and what is reviewed and carried forward; the copies stay committed so a build needs nothing more. A copy is its release, without `Cargo.lock`, examples or benches, plus its patch, and CI checks that it is (`just vendor-gpui-check`). After editing a vendored file, `just vendor-gpui-patches` writes the patches again; commit both.

## gpui-pre, gpui-pre-apple, gpui-pre-wgpu (0.3.10): shader quads

GPUI draws a fixed set of primitives, and something that changes every frame, such as the playing bars, the seek bar or the wash, costs a GPUI frame each time it moves: render, layout, prepaint, paint and a present. The patch adds one more primitive, a quad drawn by a fragment program the app supplies (`ShaderProgram`: MSL and WGSL source of one `shade` function, and an optional `prepare`), with sixteen uniforms the app writes from any thread (`ShaderUniforms`) and optionally an image from the sprite atlas. `Window::paint_shader` and `paint_shader_image` paint one.

The renderer reads the uniforms when it presents a frame, not when the frame is drawn, and hands the program `time`, the seconds since the uniforms' origin, reckoned in double precision at the present. `prepare` runs on the CPU once per quad at each present, for values every pixel would otherwise work out alike (the wash's pose and eased opacity). While any shader on screen is live, GPUI's frame callback keeps asking for refreshes and presents the last frame again on each one where a live shader's uniforms changed, or on every one for a continuous shader, which moves with `time` alone; no new frame is drawn. When none is live, the window parks as before.

A re-present costs the shaders, not the window. When a frame is drawn, the scene is split into layers at its shaders (`Scene::shader_layers`): shaders are grouped in draw order, a group ending where the next shader overlaps one in it, and every other primitive goes in the lowest layer that is after every group holding a shader it overlaps and is ordered after, and after every primitive drawn before it that it overlaps, so a menu over the bars keeps its text over it. A page's playing bars are then one group over the wash's, with the page between them as a layer. Metal and wgpu draw each layer into a texture of its own, once per drawn frame, the first opaque and the rest over a clear texture, which leaves their colours premultiplied. Each present composes the layers and the shader groups into the drawable in order, a full-screen triangle per layer. A scene whose primitives cannot be split that way (one that must be drawn both after one group and before an earlier one) is drawn whole at every present. `a_composed_present_matches_a_whole_render` in `metal_renderer.rs` checks the two give the same pixels to within a level, with a layer over the shader and without; `what_covers_a_shader_keeps_its_own_order` the same for a menu over a shader whose text is clear of it. The shader types' own tests sit beside it, since the vendored core leaves out the assets its tests read: `cargo test -p gpui-pre-apple --lib`.

Metal compiles each program the first time it is drawn, between a prelude declaring the instance and `koan_sample` and the vertex and fragment functions that call `shade`, and clips to the content mask in the fragment function. wgpu does the same in WGSL: a prelude declaring the instance, the globals and `koan_sample`, the program's `shade`, and entry points that clip to the content mask and premultiply where the surface wants it. A program is compiled the first time it is drawn under a validation error scope, so one that does not compile is logged and drawn as nothing rather than counted as the device's error. Its layers are textures of the surface's format, composed the same way; a present ensures bind groups only for the shaders' own images, so it costs the quads and not a walk of the scene. The WebGL path, which has no storage buffers, draws no shaders. `headless_renderer_draws_shader_quads`, `wgpu_composed_present_matches_a_whole_render` and `wgpu_what_covers_a_shader_keeps_its_own_order` in `wgpu_renderer.rs` check it, on Linux. Windows' DirectX renderer is not patched (it would not build against the new batch kind).

### Colour slots (#1859)

A colour that moves without a frame drawn: an app-wide table of 255 colours (`color_slots.rs`), each two colours and a track between them, which the stock quad, shadow, underline and monochrome sprite shaders read at present time (`koan_rgba` in `shaders.metal`, `shaders.wgsl` and `shaders_subpixel.wgsl`, the table bound beside the instances). A colour names a slot by a hue of 2 or more (`ColorSlot::hsla`), so no primitive changes shape and element opacity still scales it. The scene collects the slots it and each of its layers draw with (`scene.rs`), and a window presents while one moves (`window.rs`).

### Tracks (#1859)

The block of uniforms is 80 floats: 16 plain values written when they change, then eight tracks of eight. A track is one segment of a moving value (`from`, `to`, `start` in seconds of shader time, `length`, a curve, a repeat), which the program evaluates at present time through the prelude's `koan_track(u, k, time)`; `Track::at` in `shader.rs` is the same evaluation on the CPU, which a retarget samples so it starts from what is on screen, and `tracks_draw_where_the_cpu_says` in `metal_renderer.rs` holds the two together. Curves are linear, a CSS cubic Bézier (its control points as half-float pairs) and a damped spring in closed form; a track holds its end, loops or alternates. A shader presents while a track moves and once more as the last comes to rest, with no `live` or `continuous` set by hand: the app writes keyframes when its data changes and the GPU draws every frame.

`time` is reckoned at the present clock (`present_now`): now plus the lead the platform reports between encoding a frame and its showing (on macOS, the display link's output time), so motion does not jitter with encode latency, and the app's retarget reads the same clock.

## gpui-pre-macos, gpui-pre-linux (0.3.10)

GPUI's macOS and X11 backends ask for a frame on every display refresh for as long as a window is visible, and GPUI returns early from each one nothing invalidated: a window at rest wakes the main thread 60 to 120 times a second (#1609). GPUI's core already tells a backend when a frame is wanted, through `PlatformWindow::frame_waker` (when the window first becomes dirty) and `schedule_frame` (when a frame leaves work for the next, or a next-frame callback is queued). The Wayland backend implements both and asks the compositor for a frame only then; these patches do the same for the other two.

- **macOS** (`gpui-pre-macos/src/window.rs`, `display_link.rs`): the window's display link parks after three frames no one asked for. `frame_waker` and `schedule_frame` only signal a main-queue dispatch source, since GPUI can call them while the window's state is locked; its handler restarts a parked link. Visibility still starts and stops the link as before. After herdr-app's patch for gpui-pre-macos 0.3.8.
- **X11** (`gpui-pre-linux/src/linux/x11/client.rs`, `window.rs`): the refresh timer drops itself after three refreshes no one asked for and the window's refresh state becomes `Parked`. A window's waker sets a flag of its own and rings a calloop ping, so it never borrows the client's state; the ping's handler restarts the timers of parked, visible windows that asked for a frame.

## gpui-base (0.8.1): the caret's blink

gpui-base is gpui-kit's, released on gpui-kit's numbers; it draws the text fields. Its caret blinked by notifying the input's state every 500 ms, and GPUI redraws every view above one notified, so a focused field made its whole page (the album grid, a browser) render twice a second. The caret is now a shader quad (`CARET` in `blink_cursor.rs`), painted shown in its colour, whose visibility the blink writes into its uniforms before asking the window it was last painted in for a present: a blink re-presents the last frame and draws none. Starting, stopping and pausing the blink still notify, as each comes with focus or typing, which draw anyway. The OTP input, which koan does not use, keeps the notifying blink.

To move to a new GPUI release, `just vendor-gpui <version> [<gpui-kit version>]` fetches each crate's release from crates.io, checks it against the checksum the crates.io index records, and applies its patch. It stops at the first patch that does not apply, leaving `vendor/` as it was, and names the file and line. Reapply that crate's `KOAN:` hunks by hand against the release (drop any the release has taken upstream), run `just vendor-gpui-patches`, and move the pins in `Cargo.toml`.
